text:
A: Hiya! Oh, finally, Callum. You'll laugh, my son's called Callum. Every time I've seen your name come up I've thought, right, what's he left on the floor now?
B: Ha, sorry. Hello. I'm in Taunton, down in Somerset.
A: Chelmsford, Essex. Holly was saying you make bowls?
B: Er, yeah, I turn them, in my stepdad's garage. That one on the shelf behind me's one of mine. I'm a joiner really, windows and doors on old houses. The bowls are just for fun.
A: That's a proper skill though, babe. Do you sell them?
B: Not really. Give them to my mum, mostly. She's running out of shelf.
A: See, that's where you're going wrong. Craft fairs, Instagram, people pay a fortune for handmade. My friend paid ninety quid for a chopping board in Brentwood.
B: Ninety? Blimey. I'd want to see that board.
A: Oak, apparently. Lovely, to be fair. So what's the plan, are you going to go out on your own?
B: That's sort of the dream. Heritage joinery, little workshop unit somewhere. Problem is I'm useless at admin. My boss chases me for job sheets every week, and I write my cut lists on offcuts and then lose them.
A: Oh, no, hun, that's the easy bit, honestly. I'm planning the same thing, my own PT studio, renting a unit so the club stops taking a cut. And I did twenty years in recruitment, so diaries, invoices, I could do it in my sleep. You just need a system. One spreadsheet, one diary, every Friday at four, no excuses.
B: Friday at four. See, Friday at four I'm usually in the pub.
A: Then do it at three! No, seriously, or you pay someone. Half the trades I know have got a wife or a bookkeeper doing it all.
B: Not got the wife, so it'd be the bookkeeper. Er, how come you went from recruitment to fitness, then?
A: Long story. Went through a divorce, wanted a change, and I'd always been in the gym, so I thought, why not get paid for it? Did my Level 3 at forty-five. Now I've got a waiting list for my six o'clock spin.
B: Six in the morning? Fair play. I'm not really a gym person. I swim in the sea, walk on the Quantocks, that sort of thing.
A: Sea swimming? In this country? You're mad.
B: It's freezing. Went in at Lyme a couple of weeks back and couldn't feel my feet. But you come out buzzing, you know.
A: That's endorphins, that is. Same as spin, just without the hypothermia.
B: Ha, yeah. So your Callum, what's he into?
A: His phone, his mates, and leaving his washing on the bedroom floor. He's doing his A-levels, wants to go to uni, I think. Doesn't tell me much.
B: Sounds like me at seventeen. My mum'd say I'm not much different now, to be honest. I'm back living with her.
A: Oh, are you? Well, nothing wrong with that, saves you a fortune. As long as you're putting it away.
B: That's the theory.
A: Right, see, this is what I mean, you need a system! Standing order, payday, straight into...
